summary: The watch's first run. The City of Alexandria says its ban on gas leaf blowers took effect November 17. A new review of the German Lawn Research Project by Norbert Müller and Maria Ignatieva (Urban Ecosystems) reports that frequently mowed lawns support less plant diversity and wildlife value than meadows.

items.title: Alexandria, Va.: the gas leaf blower ban is in force, with citations from November 17
items.quote: Effective November 17, 2026, citations for use of gas-powered leaf blowers will be issued for residents and contractors.
items.note: Gas lawn equipment's emissions are one of the costs the site's infographic counts; here a city has banned one kind of it.

items.title: Review of the German Lawn Research Project: frequently mowed lawns support less plant diversity and wildlife value than meadows
items.quote: Due to the high cutting frequency, lawns generally support lower plant biodiversity and provide less value for wildlife than meadows.
items.note: Bears on the backlog's "Lawns support almost no insect life": a peer-reviewed review on plants and wildlife value generally, not insects specifically.
